body:
`insight:marks-taking-the-temperature-2023` | confidence: verified | date: 2023-07-10

Memo of 10 Jul 2023. His son Andrew: his calls were right 'because you did it five times in 50 years' - Jan 2000 (TMT), 2004-07 (credit excess), late 2008 (buy), Mar 2012 (buy amid equity disillusionment; S&P then returned 16.5%/yr 2012-2021), Mar 2020 (buy; 'The bottom is the day before the recovery begins'). 'Once in a while - once or twice a decade, perhaps - markets go so high or so low that the argument for action is compelling and the probability of being right is high'; otherwise 'one key is to avoid making macro calls too often.' Edge does not come from data: 'readily available quantitative data regarding the past and present can't hold the secret' - 'The key lies in understanding prevailing investor psychology.' Checklist (paraphrased headings, quotes verbatim): engage in pattern recognition (cycles 'fluctuate in ways that approach dependability'); cycles stem from 'excesses and corrections'; watch for 'things can only get better' ('there's no price too high') or 'things can only get worse' ('a sale at any price is a good sale'); in extremes 'the secret to making money lies in contrarianism, not conformity' but 'most of the time, the consensus is as close to right as most individuals can get'; to be contrarian know '(a) what the herd is doing, (b) why it's doing it, (c) what's wrong with it, and (d) what should be done instead and why'; 'Resist your own emotionality'; on illogical propositions, 'See something; do something.' 2004-07 tell: 'If deals like this can get done ... there's something wrong with the market.'

Sources:
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/insights/memo/taking-the-temperature

body:
- The pre-registered public rule is **not a proven edge**. The honest read is a *possible* weak right-tail tilt
  (mean +4 to +7%/yr in every variant, CI touching 0, median negative).
- Use: a **research-queue trigger**. Promoter open-market buying ≥ ₹1 cr in a ₹500–2,000 cr company is a reason to read the
  filings (pledge status, capex cycle, order book). It is not a buy signal. This matches L14.
- If tested again, pre-register *one* refinement and test it out of sample (e.g. signals 2017–2020 or 2025–26): promoter-only,
  ₹500–2,000 cr, **no pledge outstanding**, first promoter buy in ≥ 3 years (CMP-style "opportunistic"), plus a sector-matched
  control. Primary metric unchanged.

body:
- Pledge comes from one June-quarter SHP per year (0–15 months stale, pre-registered). This dilutes the flags, so the
  true halving gaps are probably a little larger.
- S2 fires on 20% of events, including banks and NBFCs (their interest cover is structurally < 1.5x). The verdicts
  are the same with financials excluded.
- Restated standalone screener annuals (holdco debt under-flagged); weekly closes; price returns only; dead firms
  are a 39% sample and most failures were below the ₹500 cr floor (L31).
- Halving is about the path, and events overlap (the same firm appears in several quarters). The quarter bootstrap
  handles the time clustering but not the firm clustering, so the halving CIs are somewhat too narrow.
- 2018–21 includes the IL&FS/NBFC squeeze and COVID: halving rates there are about 2–3× those of 2022–25.

body:
| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `common.py` | Cache layout, the Indian fiscal calendar, date parsing |
| `fetch.py` | Pulls the NSE announcement list with the short UA `Mozilla/5.0` and filters it to transcript PDFs (catches typos such as "Trancript"; skips .zip files). Downloads **only the PDFs in the date range**, which fixes pilot lesson 1. Runs `pdftotext -layout`, detects the call date (the "held on …" date, never the quarter-end date) and the quarter. Flags PDFs that look scanned (fewer than 1,500 words; these need OCR). |
| `turns.py` | Splits the text into speaker turns: management, analyst, moderator or host. Speaker roles are resolved in this order: (1) the cover-page roster, merged across all of the company's calls, with fuzzy matching (handles "Parmjit Soni", "Paramjit Sonis", "Aditya Dujari :", dropped middle names); (2) generic labels such as "Management:"; (3) analysts named in the moderator's announcement; (4) a content vote. Each turn records `role_basis` so it can be audited. Turns are tagged opening / qa / closing. Removes the cover letter, page headers, safe-harbour text and operator housekeeping. Optional `rosters.json` maps `{SYMBOL: [names]}`. |
| `candidates.py` | Rule-based extraction of forward-looking sentences. Signals: guidance verbs; numbers with %, ₹/INR/cr, tonnes, days; qualitative magnitudes ("mid-teens", "double-digit", "flat"); timelines (FY28, Q3FY27, H2, "next year", "in 2-3 years", "end of the year", month names). A metric may come from the analyst's question when the answer only says "it". Also catches "Yes, absolutely" answers that endorse a target the analyst stated. Output is `candidates.jsonl` with quote, speaker, call date, section, volunteered flag, the question being answered, numbers, and a deadline resolved with the **later-date rule** (`assumed` explains each choice). Tier A = strong, tier B = directional. |
| `llm_extract_prompt.md` | Prompt template for the LLM confirmation and structuring step. The output schema matches `score.py`'s input: measure vocabulary, period, target_low/high, comparator, deadline rules, `chain_key`, `restates_earlier`, `acknowledges_revision`. |
| `llm_extract.py` | Runs the template call by call, oldest first. Feeds the `chain_key`s already used into each later prompt so the same target keeps the same key. Validates the output and assigns ids. Caches raw output in `llm/`. |
| `llm_candour_prompt.md` | Optional per-shortfall prompt: "was this miss admitted unprompted?" |
| `financials.py` | Fetches the screener.in consolidated page with curl (cached for 3 days) and parses the quarterly, P&L, balance-sheet, cash-flow and ratio tables. A CSV can be supplied instead or as an override. |
| `score.py` | Auto-scores financial promises and builds the supersedes chains (details below). |
| `report.py` | MCS, weighted delivery ratio, hit rate, candour index; breakdowns by category, driver (cycle vs execution), specificity, volunteered/prompted, year said and speaker; markdown ledger; memdb seed. |
| `validate.py` | Compares pipeline output with a manual ledger (recall/precision, field agreement, status agreement, goalposts). |
| `run.py` | Orchestrator. |
| `ar_fetch.py` | AR mode: last N annual reports (NSE), text extracted, PDFs deleted; manifest dated at submission. |
| `ar_sections.py` | AR mode: forward-looking zone -> management "turns" (two-column split, tables row by row, FY/month normalisation). |
| `ar_run.py` | AR mode orchestrator: candidates -> rule promises -> next-report evidence -> score -> report, plus asset tracker and flags. |
| `regress_concall.py` | Proves concall-mode outputs are byte-identical to a reference git revision. |
